title: 25-26. THEY PUT HIM IN A COFFIN IN EGYPT

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "And Joseph made the Israelites swear an oath and said, 'God will surely come to your aid, and then you must carry my bones up from this place.' So Joseph died at the age of a hundred and ten. And after they embalmed him, he was placed in a coffin in Egypt." — Gen 50:25-26 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The book of Genesis ends with a coffin in Egypt.

That is a strange ending for a book that began with light and life and a garden. It closes with a body in a box in a foreign country. Everything is unfinished — the promise unfulfilled, the family far from home, and four centuries of hardship ahead that nobody in the room can see.

But that coffin was a statement of faith. Joseph refused burial in Egypt. He gave instructions to carry his bones out, because he was certain his people were going home. For four hundred years that coffin sat among the Israelites as a standing reminder: we are not staying here.

And they kept the promise. Moses took Joseph's bones out of Egypt (Ex 13:19), and Joshua buried them at Shechem in the land God had given (Josh 24:32).

Genesis ends unfinished on purpose. It is the first chapter of a much longer story — one that runs through the exodus, the kings and the prophets, and arrives at a manger, a cross, and an empty tomb.

The last coffin in Scripture's story is empty. Because Christ has risen, ours will be too (1 Cor 15:20).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What unfinished thing in your life are you tempted to see as the end of the story?
2. How does the resurrection of Christ change how you view death?
3. What "bones" of faith are you leaving behind as a witness to those after you?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that no story of Yours ends in a coffin. Because Christ is risen, my hope is secure. Help me live as someone who knows this is not the end. Amen.
